paper_candidates.title: The increase in cell volume and nuclear number of the koji-fungus Aspergillus oryzae contributes to its high enzyme productivity.
paper_candidates.authors: Itani A, Motomura H, Oda K, Yamashita H, Sakai K, Kusumoto KI, Shigeto S, Ichikawa T, Mubarak HM, Fukuma T, Katayama T, Maruyama JI, Masuo S, Takaya N, Takeshita N.
paper_candidates.abstract: While the ratio of nuclei to cell volume is well regulated, it remains largely unexplored in multinucleate organisms. The koji-fungus Aspergillus oryzae, traditionally used in Japanese brewing and fermentation for over a thousand years, is now widely utilized in modern biotechnology as a host for enzyme production. We discovered that, over time in culture, hyphae become thicker, resulting in a tenfold increase in cell volume, and the number of nuclei in hyphal cells also increases tenfold, exceeding 200. The increase in cell volume and nuclear number is unique among the investigated Aspergillus species and correlates with its high enzyme production capabilities. Since nuclear number and cell volume are correlated, both must increase simultaneously for either to expand. Our analyses identified genetic factors and nutritional environmental signals involved in each of these increases. Increases in nuclear number and cell volume were also observed in other fungi bred for industrial use. This study not only deepens our understanding of the evolutionary processes that promote high enzyme productivity through fungal breeding, but also provides insights into the molecular mechanisms regulating cell volume and nuclear number in multinucleate organisms.

curated_conditions.medium: minimal medium (MM) agar overlaid with sterilized cellophane
curated_conditions.carbon_source: maltose (1%, stated for MM elsewhere in the paper; not restated for the RNA-seq cultures)
curated_conditions.recombinant_background: wild_type (RIB40 reference strain; hyphae with increased nuclei)
curated_conditions.production_context: nuclear number / cell volume / enzyme secretion study of koji mold
curated_conditions.metadata_source: BioProject PRJDB19992 (DRA DRP012531, Univ. of Tsukuba), article 'The increase in cell volume and nuclear number of the koji-fungus Aspergillus oryzae contributes to its high enzyme productivity' (eLife 2025, doi 10.7554/eLife.107043, PMC12456952; data statement 'RNA-seq data deposited in DDBJ as BioProject PRJDB19992'). Methods: sterilized cellophane placed on agar plates, conidia inoculated, cultured at 30 C for 3 days, frozen and ground, RNeasy Mini Kit; 36 bp paired-end reads on Illumina NextSeq 500 (University of Tsukuba). The paper describes the medium only as minimal medium (MM) with or without 1% yeast extract; 1% maltose is the carbon source stated for MM in its protein-secretion assays, not restated for the RNA-seq cultures. BioSample SAMD00876706 sample_name 'RIB40MM'. One library per strain x medium, no biological replicates.

Methods: sterilized membrane slides immersed in MM liquid, conidia inoculated, static culture at 30 C for 3 days; thick and thin hyphae cut out with a PALM MicroBeam laser microdissection system (500-700 sections per sample), RNeasy Mini Kit; 150 bp paired-end reads on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 (Takara Bio). Sequencing platform and read length differ from the cellophane-culture libraries of this BioProject.
